title: The 13 most haunted Airbnbs in the U.S.A.
excerpt: Do Halloween right at one of these spine-tingling stays
content:
Photograph: Airbnb

Gothic architecture, vintage interiors and a high probability of existential dread at 3 AM. Book one of these stays—if you dare

Tuesday September 15 2026

Share

If you’re a fan of all things that go bump in the night, read on. These scarily good Airbnbs put the “boo” in booking. We’ve scoured the eeriest corners of the U.S.A. to track down the most haunted Airbnbs, which includes everything from shadow-draped castles to old, creepy mansions packed with creaking floorboards, and the possibility of an uninvited roommate. 

You might not exactly rest in peace, but you will get a front-row seat to the supernatural. A word to the wise, though—these legendary spots book up faster than a ghost vanishing through a wall, so secure your stay ASAP.

Updated for 2026: With spooky season on the horizon, we’ve added a few more of the most haunted properties in the U.S. to our list. Enter if you dare.

The U.S.A.’s most haunted Airbnbs, at a glance:

  • 🩸 Best for paranormal activity: the Civil War field hospital in Gettysburg, PA
  • 👻 Best for shy ghosts and garden strolls: the dead girl’s bedroom in NOLA
  • 🏚️ Best for Salem Witch Trial history: Haunted Henry’s house in Salem
  • 🏔️ Best for large groups: the haunted brothel in Victor, CO
  • 🌵 Best for off-grid stargazing: the ghost town in Terlingua, TX

Who makes the cut? While we might not stay in every Airbnb featured, we’ve based our list on top reviews, hosts, and amenities to find you the best stays. This article includes affiliate links. These links have no influence on our editorial content. For more information, see our affiliate guidelines.

Frequently asked questions about staying in a haunted Airbnb

No. Every listing here is upfront that ghostly activity is reported by guests and hosts, not promised. Most say experiences are unpredictable and some guests leave without noticing anything unusual at all. 

That depends on the individual listing’s cancellation policy, not on how spooked you get. Check the specific policy before booking, and if you’re prone to getting rattled, a shorter first stay is a safer bet than a week-long one.

Physically, yes, these are normal, well-reviewed properties with the same safety standards as any other Airbnb. Whether it’s the right vibe for a child depends more on how they’ll react to ghost stories and old houses than on any real risk. A few listings on this list are pet-friendly, so check individual amenities if you’re bringing an animal along.

Haunted Airbnbs in the U.S.

1. Best for testing your nerve: a night in a real former morgue

Location: Ozark, Missouri.

Welcome to the Historic Morgue. This nationally recognized building has had many lives, serving as a morgue, funeral home, church and museum. The current decor plays with that history, scattering antique funeral pieces in with a modern twist throughout. It’s set up loft-style with a king bed, a full-size bed, a single and an antique settee all sharing one room, plus a claw-foot tub from the early 1900s in the bathroom. Numerous professional paranormal research teams have spent the night here and reported unexplained activity, and the host provides some of their own investigation equipment, a spirit box, EMF detector and dowsing rods, if you fancy doing your own digging.

Time Out tip: The host is upfront that there are no refunds if you leave mid-stay, ghost related or otherwise, so this one’s for guests who are unfazed by hauntaunts. It’s also a short walk to downtown Ozark and the Finley River, worth pairing with a daytime wander if the morgue gets to be a bit much.

Sleeps: One bedroom, six beds (a king, a double, a single and a sofa). Sleeps 6 guests.

Price: From $221 a night.

2. Best for Stranger Things immersion: the Byers house filming location

Location: Fayetteville, Georgia.

Are you ready to step into the Upside Down? This is the actual filming location for the Byers house from Stranger Things, and it’s been transformed into a fully immersive stay inspired by Hawkins circa 1983. It took over a year and dozens of fans and professionals to curate every VHS tape, vinyl record and board game inside and the result is detail-obsessed, right down to the interactive Christmas light wall modelled on the Byers’ living room and a CRT TV playing period-accurate tapes. It’s a fan-driven project and not an official Netflix property, but the team behind it are clearly obsessed with getting it right.

Time Out tip: It’s just 15 to 20 minutes from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta Airport and 10 minutes from Trilith Studios, so it’s an easy add-on if you’re already in Atlanta. Just know all guests and vehicles need to be registered with the host ahead of arrival, and there’s a strict no-parties policy backed up by noise monitors and security cameras.

Sleeps: Three bedrooms, six beds (a king, a queen, and an Upside-Down-themed bunk room with four bunks), two bathrooms. Sleeps 6 guests.

Price: From $1,225 a night.

3. Best for large groups and Wild West ghost hunters: the haunted brothel

Location: Victor, Colorado

After a fire in 1899 destroyed this Victorian-era brothel, casino, and saloon, the space was rebuilt and meticulously restored, bringing spirited supernatural stories. Legend claims the Victorian Gothic building’s electrical wiring was done by Nikolas Tesla. Its bay windows, oak doors, 12- to 15-foot ceilings, and hardwood stairs are all original. The ghost who lives here is said to be a former miner who died in a gunfight. Equally creepy are some of the taxidermy and art the current owners have added.

Time Out tip: The building sits right next to the Victor Lowell Thomas Museum in this Rocky Mountain gold rush town. It’s worth a wander if you want the full backstory before you spend the night in a home that has one of its own.

Sleeps: Seven bedrooms, ten beds plus two sofas. Sleeps up to 16 guests.

Perks: The Rocky Mountains right on your doorstep in the heart of Victor, Colorado, dedicated workspace, pets allowed, free on-site parking.

Price: From $1,100 a night.

4. Best for history buffs and paranormal activity: the Civil War field hospital

Location: Gettysburg, Pennsylvania

The barn and farmhouse on this historic property were both used as a Confederate field hospital after the Battle of Gettysburg, so you can only imagine how many spirits are milling about. Prepare yourself for the possibility of spotting multiple apparitions: the host of David Stewart Farm says she’s seen plenty over the years, but promises they’re all friendly. Guests have reported hearing footsteps and seeing men dressed in Confederate soldier uniforms. The bedroom itself is decked out in period decor to really put you in the 19th-century frame of mind, if that’s your style.

Time Out tip: The property sits on 100 acres with hiking and mountain biking trails and a pond stocked with bass, sunfish and catfish, so bring a rod if you fancy it. Just know you'll be sharing the kitchen and living room with the host, her dog and five cats, so it's not a fully private stay.

Sleeps: Two bedrooms, three beds (a queen and two twins). Sleeps up to 4 guests.

Perks: 100 acres of trails, fishing pond, fire pit, large deck, coffee and tea provided each morning.

Price: From $156 dollars a night.

5. Best for murder mystery dinners: the mysterious manor

Location: Saint Paul, Minnesota.

Built in 1883, The Manor is a mysterious castle in St. Paul brimming with creepy vibes. Formerly the St. Paul Art Gallery, this Victorian home is palatial—perfect for spirits and paranormal activity. Furnished with oddities and curiosities, The Manor may be haunted—or it might not be, depending on your perception—but it’s a popular spot for rituals, murder mystery dinners, and paranormal investigations like one undertaken in 1969 by a trio of journalists at the Pioneer Press.

Time Out tip: The host also books the property for daytime paranormal investigations, ceremonies and photo shoots, so if a simple overnight stay isn’t spooky enough, ask about renting the space for an event too. Just know you’ll be sharing the kitchen and bathroom with the host, and government ID verification is required before booking.

Sleeps: One queen bed, shared bathroom. Sleeps up to 2 guests.

Perks: Enclosed courtyard with fire pit, in-suite laundry with sanitising functions, whirlpool tub, dedicated workspace, off-street parking inside a gated compound.

Price: From $125 a night.

6. Best for luxury group stays: the gothic castle

Location: Ellicott City, Maryland.

Renting the Lilburn Mansion near Baltimore will get you two bedrooms, a ballroom, library, a pool and tons of outdoor space. It will also get you a haunted roommate or two. After a fire destroyed the original 1857 property, ’the castle’, as the owners called it, went through an extensive restoration. But the stone manor’s spectral residents didn’t much appreciate the changes, and a string of bad luck followed its living ones—including the death of a child as well as the family’s patriarch. Recently, guests have reported plenty of ghostly activity in the mansion, like the time someone spotted a child hanging from a chandelier.

Time Out tip: The house has hosted productions for Discovery Channel, A&E and several feature films, so keep an eye out for the kind of details a film crew would love, all that original stonework and the ballroom especially. It’s walking distance to historic downtown Ellicott City if you want a break from the ghost stories.

Sleeps: Four bedrooms, four beds, 5.5 bathrooms. Base rate covers up to 4 guests; additional guests are $100 per night each.

Perks: Outdoor pool, private garden and grounds, in-unit washer and dryer, free parking, five-minute walk to historic downtown shops and restaurants.

Price: From $1200 a night.

7. Best for budget travelers and pet owners: the mysterious gingerbread house

Location: Bisbee, Arizona

This adorable cottage in Bisbee, Arizona has all the charm you’d want out of an affordable Airbnb retreat—and some mysterious ghostly activity to boot. The listing doesn’t go into much detail about what exactly haunts the gingerbread house, but repeated episodes of odd, unexplained mischief have been reported (though nothing scary or malevolent... so far). Luckily, the place is pet-friendly, so feel free to bring along Fido to protect you from whatever awaits in Bisbee.

Time Out tip: There’s no wifi or TV here by design. The host has kept it a step back in time, right down to a 1919 Brunswick phonograph she’ll play records on by request.

Sleeps: Two bedrooms, three beds (a double, plus a futon that sleeps two). Sleeps up to 5 guests.

Perks: Fully fenced yard, organic bedding and toiletries throughout, porch swing and glider seat, pet friendly with no fees, four steps up rather than a steep staircase.

Price: From $150 a night.

8. Best for shy ghosts and garden strolls: the dead girl’s bedroom

Location: New Orleans, Louisiana (Garden District)

New Orleans has its fair share of haunted attractions, but nothing sounds scarier than the idea of sharing a bedroom with a young ghost in a yellow dress. Although the 130-year-old Parks-Bowman Mansion in NOLA’s Garden District offers multiple rooms, there’s only one room that’s supposedly haunted by a shy ghost, thought to be the youngest daughter of the house’s original owners, who was buried on the grounds in the 1890s after her untimely death. Of course, you may or may not actually encounter the youngster or hear her pacing the grounds with a slight limp, softly humming lullabies, or hiding pairs of glasses.

Time Out tip: You’re a short walk from Lafayette Cemetery, Commander’s Palace and the St Charles Avenue streetcar line, and if you’re visiting for Mardi Gras, you’ll be steps from the parade route. Just know cooking isn’t permitted in the kitchen, you get access for drinkware and ice only, so plan to eat out.

Sleeps: One queen bed, dedicated bathroom (private room in a shared house). Sleeps up to 2 guests.

Perks: Year-round heated outdoor pool, private third-floor balcony, complimentary morning coffee, secure on-street parking, mini fridge and cable TV in the room.

Price: From $197 a night.

9. Best for vintage spooky charm: the Queen Anne Hotel

Location: San Francisco, California (Pacific Heights)

San Francisco’s Queen Anne Hotel is one of those ‘Oh that place? HAUNTED,’ properties. And the Victorian era hotel certainly looks the part (why it is called ‘Queen Anne’ and not ‘Queen Victoria’ is slightly confusing but we’ll stop splitting straws). Originally a Girls’ Finishing School, the place is full of gothicky, deep-hued furnishings and opportunities to, for example, take sherry in the parlor. Its otherworldly resident is said to be the former Headmistress. Better make sure you’re not misbehaving, eh?

Time Out tip: Evening tea and sherry service happens nightly in the fireplace parlor and library, complete with a baby grand piano, so time your check-in so you don't miss out on the hotel's best ritual.

Sleeps: One bedroom, one king bed, private bathroom. Sleeps 2 guests.

Perks: Complimentary continental breakfast, evening tea and sherry service, outdoor courtyard, self-parking, five-minute walk to Lafayette Park.

Price: From $281 a night.

10. Best for couples: the 18th century cottage

Location: Savannah, Georgia (Landmark Historic District)

Step back in time at Laura’s Cottage, located in Savannah’s Landmark Historic District. There you’ll be able to sip a cocktail in the front porch rocking chairs with Laura, a ghost that haunts this small refuge built in 1799. Not much is known about the apparition, but it’s said that she once lived in the cottage and could often be seen tending the garden. Reports of paranormal activity include windows opening (on their own!) and lights mysteriously turning off and on, so don’t bank on getting much rest.

Time Out tip: It’s a favorite stop on local ghost tours, so if you want the full backstory on Laura beyond what the hosts can tell you, book one that passes by River Street,  which is just a five-minute walk from the door.

Sleeps: One bedroom, three beds (a queen plus two twins). Sleeps up to 4 guests.

Perks: Free private parking, in-unit washer and dryer, private patio, fast wifi, breakfast provided.

Price: From $370 a night.

11. Best for off-grid stargazing: the ghost town

Location: Terlingua, Texas

One-up America’s most haunted Airbnbs by staying in a Texas ghost town. Once a mining boomtown, just about everyone but the ghosts have long since moved on from Terlingua. In this 100-year-old miner’s casita, you’ll find a bedroom, living room, kitchen, and outdoor bathroom (a scary situation in itself). Watch for paranormal activity from the porch of this stacked limestone cabin, which luckily has lovely views of Big Bend National Park’s mountains and badlands.

Time Out tip: There’s no wifi on site but if you need it, the Starlight Restaurant, La Posada coffee shop and The Venga nearby all have it. Big Bend National Park's west entrance is just 10 minutes away, so it’s worth pairing the ghost stories with a hike.

Sleeps: One bedroom, one bed, one bathroom (separate, a few steps out the back door). Sleeps up to 2 guests.

Perks: Dual porches with mountain views, fire pit, single-level with no stairs, free parking, walkable to local restaurants.

Price: From $235 a night.

12. Best for Salem Witch Trial history: Haunted Henry’s house

Location: Salem, Massachusetts (McIntire District)

It’s fitting that the town where the 17th century Salem Witch Trials took place would have plenty of historic haunted mansions. The Henry Derby House is no exception. Built for tailor Henry Derby, the 19th-century Greek Revival rental home is now owned by Phil Marchand, who grew up in the haunted home. He and others have heard footsteps from the third floor, have been startled by bumps in the night and many guests have spotted the ghost of a teenage girl with long hair.

Time Out tip: It’s a five-minute walk to the Peabody Essex Museum and a block from Salem’s shops and restaurants, but this isn’t a party house, guests must sign a rental agreement, and anyone staying overnight needs to be listed on it, so plan your group accordingly.

Sleeps: Seven bedrooms, eight beds (one king, two queens, five singles), four bathrooms. Sleeps up to 12 guests.

Perks: Pellet stove for cooler evenings, private garden, free parking, in-unit washer and dryer, dedicated workspace.

Price: From $1,306 a night.

13. Best for ghost investigators and TV show fans: the Magnolia B&B

Location: Seguin, Texas (Historic Downtown District)

Another well and truly haunted property in Texas, the Magnolia B&B has been featured on a host of spooky television series. In fact, it’s such a big presence in ghostly hotel circles, it’s even got its own book on the subject. The place itself was built in 1850 as a frontier-hotel-stagecoach-stop-saloon-restaurant-brothel (quite the multipurpose venue). The current owners really lean into its status as a place to meet those who dwell in the afterlife, giving you ample opportunities for learning lots about your spooky neighbors.

Time Out tip: Filming for social media isn’t allowed on the second floor without written permission in advance, so if you’re planning a ghost-hunting video, message the hosts before you book. For an extra $20 a person, you can also add a guided daytime tour of the downstairs and basement, which isn’t otherwise included in your stay.

Sleeps: Two bedrooms, two beds (one king, one queen), one bathroom. Sleeps 4 guests (a fifth can be added for an extra fee).

Perks: Central Park steps away, non-cooking kitchen with microwave and mini-fridge, continental breakfast included, dedicated workspace, free parking.

Price: From $206 a night.
